subject: Payload patterns & pilot plan for ParcelFlow — throughput and streaming checks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: payload patterns & pilot plan (throughput + streaming)

Hi Tom — great chat today, thanks for walking through ParcelFlow's realtime order update flow. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size the pilot: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct anything):
- Baseline steady QPS: ~6 QPS across your APIs to start, with major regional concentration east-coast US.
- Burst behavior: short crests ~3x baseline, occasional sustained peaks ~8–10x during promotions (rare, minutes-long).
- Typical response length: ~120–180 tokens (median ~150).
- Streaming usage: order-status stream used for real-time updates, ~30% of calls; expected concurrency for streams ~120 simultaneous users during peak.
- Latency target: you indicated P95 < 250ms for interactive flows; internal ops prefer planning for 200ms p95 if possible.

Immediate asks / artifacts we requested on call:
1) Sample token/latency traces for a busy 1-hour window (CSV or JSON) — helps us validate batching profile and KV cache hit assumptions.
2) A short list of endpoints that will use streaming vs request/response (we only need a quick mapping).
3) Any hard SLA constraints (e.g. payments vs non-critical notifications).

What Redwood recommends for pilot sizing (high level):
- Start with capacity to sustain ~2x baseline (so 12 QPS sustained) with burst headroom to 36 QPS for short crests.
- Optimize for token throughput: assume 150 tokens/response * 12 QPS = 1,800 tokens/sec sustained; plan for 6k tokens/sec burst envelope.
- Streaming capacity: reserve for 120 concurrent streams; tune windowing and per-connection batching to keep tail latency low.

Next steps we agreed: 
- You share sample traces and endpoint mappings (attachment stub: parcelflow_token_hist.csv)
- We'll do an internal sizing pass and share a lightweight canary plan (Marissa to lead the technical session)
- Target pilot start: week of Oct 18 (flexible)

Thanks — I put Marissa on Cc to schedule the deep tech session.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
[Attachment: parcelflow_token_hist.csv (csv)]

Date: 2026-10-04T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: payload patterns & pilot plan (throughput + streaming)

Thanks Priya — this aligns with what we discussed. Answers inline: 

> Baseline steady QPS: ~6 QPS
Confirmed. Region distribution: 75% east US, 15% west US, 10% EU.

> Burst behavior: short crests ~3x baseline, occasional sustained peaks ~8–10x
Yes — cresting to ~18 QPS is the norm for short marketing pushes. We see the rare promo that holds around 50 QPS for 5–20 minutes, historically twice per quarter.

> Typical response length: ~120–180 tokens
We measured median ~150 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens for verbose order notes.

> Streaming usage: ~30% of calls; concurrency ~120
Correct. Streams are persistent websockets for order updates; typical TTL per session ~10–15 minutes.

> Latency target: P95 < 250ms (ops prefers 200ms)
We'd like to aim for 200ms P95 for customer-facing status updates; internal dashboards can tolerate up to 400ms.

Attachments: attaching a small export of traces from last weekend (pf_sample_traces.json). Let me know if you need richer context (headers, timestamp resolution).

Pilot: happy with a 2-week canary starting mid-Oct. I'll introduce you to our technical lead, Elena, in a follow-up.

— Tom
Tom Hargreaves
Head of Platform Engineering, ParcelFlow

Priya — reviewing Tom's traces now. Quick internal notes / proposed technical approach: 

1) Sizing assumptions (first-draft):
   - Sustained workload: 12 QPS * 150 tokens = ~1.8k tokens/sec.
   - Burst envelope: plan for 6k tokens/sec headroom (covers up to x3 sustained bursts and short promo crests).
   - Streaming: 120 concurrent sessions -> treat as long-lived connections with per-connection amortized overhead; reserve ~10% additional CPU for connection churn.

2) Runtime knobs to reduce p95: 
   - Continuous batching window: 15–25ms depending on measured inter-arrival; Marissa suggests 20ms to start.
   - KV prefix caching for repeated contexts (order templates) — should reduce token generation by ~15–25% for our sample.
   - Aggressive KV cache TTL for session-level keys during streaming sessions.

3) Canary plan: 
   - Phase 0 (dry-run): run in our staging cluster with live traffic replay from sample traces to validate latency envelope.
   - Phase 1 (canary): route 2% traffic for 48 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99, token cost, and backpressure.
   - Phase 2 (ramp): if metrics hold, move to 20% for 3 days, then full pilot.

4) Initial infra ask:
   - Temporary dedicated pool (2 A100-equivalent nodes) for pilot; we can simulate different quantization profiles in staging.

I attached a quick sizing workbook (sizing_calc_v1.xlsx) with the math cells. Priya, can you confirm ParcelFlow is comfortable with the Phase 1 canary percentages and the pilot timing (week of Oct 18)? Markus — FYI on the dedicated pool ask; happy to sync if you want to adjust SLA ladder.

— Marissa
